transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-12 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Sarah (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood CSM), Maya (GreenLeaf Head of ML), Ethan (Platform Eng), Priya (Security), Liam (Product), Zoe (Ops)

Summary (auto): Quick review of POC metrics, then deep-dive into rollout plan: cutover, canary approach, monitoring/alerts, runbooks, rollback.

[00:00] Sarah (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: 1) review last week's results, 2) go over the canary plan and cutover checklist, 3) monitoring and runbooks, and 4) actions. sound good?
[00:18] Maya (GreenLeaf): yep sounds good. we ran the daily traffic split tests, saw latency p50 stable, p95 spiky around peak, but overall maybe good for canary.
[00:32] Daniel (Redwood SE): yeah the p95 spikes correspond to the long-context queries we saw; we suggested a small config tweak to batching and kv cache TTL last week which helped reduce cost but might increase a few ms in tail under contention.
[00:48] Ethan (GreenLeaf): quick question on that, if we roll those config changes to canary will that affect accuracy? we can't have user-facing regressions.
[01:05] Daniel (Redwood SE): good call, the change is conservative — it prioritizes latency SLO for short queries and keeps long context intact. we should include a quality check step in the canary: run the same eval prompt set and check A/B delta on our thresholds (no more than 1% top-line degradation).
[01:28] Priya (Security): From compliance side we need to confirm data residency for logs and whether KV cache contents are considered PII. also SSO test accounts need to be ready.
[01:44] Ravi (Redwood CSM): we'll include a KMS/retention checklist in the security artifacts. i'll send SOC2 and the architecture diagram after this call.
[02:02] Liam (Product): thinking about cutover window: we prefer midnight PST on a Tuesday, but open to alternative. can we do a staged cutover with canary first?
[02:20] Sarah (Redwood AE): yes staged cutover is the plan — start with 5% traffic to Redwood Dedicated (pilot cluster) for 24 hours, monitor key metrics, then 25% for next 48 hours, then final migration. we also recommend automated rollback if error-rate > 0.5% or p95 increases 50% vs baseline.
[02:45] Zoe (Ops): what alerts are you proposing? paging for SE on specifics.
[02:52] Daniel (Redwood SE): we suggest alert thresholds: error-rate > 0.3% (warning), > 0.5% (critical), p95 increase > 30% (warning), >50% (critical). add observability on model tokens per request, cache hit rate, and GPU utilization.
[03:20] Maya (GreenLeaf): and for quality signals — we need automatic sampling of 50 requests per hour to run through the eval set and a human review backlog.
[03:35] Daniel (Redwood SE): agree. we'll wire in the quality monitor to flag any regression and send to slack #ai-quality. recommend blocking rollout on any regression over 1% for >2 consecutive hours.
[03:52] Priya (Security): also SSO — we need to test SAML with our identity provider. when can we get a test account?
[04:05] Ethan (GreenLeaf): we can provision a test account by Friday. i'll note action item.
[04:12] Sarah (Redwood AE): great. i'll summarize the canary runbook tonight. daniel can you take the technical draft?
[04:18] Daniel (Redwood SE): yeah i'll draft the canary steps: pre-checks, traffic split commands, monitoring dashboards to watch, rollback commands, and post-cutover validation.
[04:30] Liam (Product): about A/B test — we want to run feature-flag driven A/B on a subset of customers rather than pure traffic split for a week to validate business metrics. is that supported?
[04:44] Daniel (Redwood SE): yes you can route by header or user cohort. we'll recommend a cohort-based A/B for product metrics (engagement) and still keep a separate canary for infra stability.
[04:58] Maya (GreenLeaf): timeline check — how long to get everything ready? we want canary next week.
[05:06] Sarah (Redwood AE): propose scheduling the canary window for 2026-05-20 02:00-04:00 UTC (which is overnight PST as you mentioned). sound doable?
[05:18] Ethan (GreenLeaf): that works for ops team.
[05:24] Priya (Security): need to ensure logging retention and KMS keys configured before that date.
[05:30] Ravi (Redwood CSM): i'll send security artifacts and KMS checklist by 2026-05-13.
[05:37] Maya (GreenLeaf): quick nit — what about fallback model variants if the main model has issues?
[05:45] Daniel (Redwood SE): good point. we'll include automatic fallback to a lower-latency quantized model with a simpler prompt template; that will be in the runbook as a secondary path. recommend limiting fallback to 10% traffic and only as an automated failover.
[06:05] Liam (Product): are there cost implications for the staged rollout we should signal to finance?
[06:12] Sarah (Redwood AE): minimal incremental cost for a short canary, but Dedicated reserved capacity will be billed — we'll share a short pricing note.
[06:25] Zoe (Ops): who triggers the final cutover?
[06:30] Sarah (Redwood AE): final cutover triggers: ops + product + redwood rep sign-off after 72 hours of 25% stability and quality checks green. we'll capture approval in the cutover checklist.
[06:45] Ethan (GreenLeaf): can you also send the template for the post-mortem / post-cutover report?
[06:52] Ravi (Redwood CSM): yes i'll include a template.
[07:05] Sarah (Redwood AE): ok let's recap actions and owners. Daniel will draft canary + cutover runbook, Ravi sends security docs, Maya/Ethan validate SSO, Ethan builds baseline dashboard. we'll meet after canary to review results.
[07:22] Maya (GreenLeaf): thanks everyone.
[07:26] Sarah (Redwood AE): thanks, meeting end.
notes: References: internal deck (link shared in chat), security artifacts to be shared by CSM. Customer requested canary window 2026-05-20. Quality thresholds: <=1% top-line degradation, automated rollback on error-rate >0.5%.
